findings.F1: The book's deepest fall, -16.8% over 339 days in windows w16 to w18, came while it held shorts that had drifted away from the lows. In w16 to w18, in-position bars more than 5% above the coin's 30-day low lost a summed -0.95 over 127 bars (mean -0.74% a day). The 16 bars still near the low earned +0.015. Holding the coins rose a summed +0.91 over the same stretch.
findings.F2: Inside the idea's falling calm regime, signal cases near the 30-day low carry the effect and those that have bounced do not.
findings.F3: Being near the 30-day low is not an effect on its own, so it can repair the idea.
findings.F4: Near the low, the effect stays graded by the volume shrink. The stronger-forecast half earns +6.0% (t 3.39, 40 cases) against +1.6% (t 1.10, 39 cases) for the weaker half.
findings.F5: Keeping only the book's positions on bars within 5% of the 30-day low fixes both failing measures in the rebuilt gross book.
findings.F6: The book's losses come from shorts held after a bounce.
findings.F7: The size against cost is not the obstacle. The total move per case is +0.46% against a 0.19% trade cost, and near the low the total move is +3.1% per case. The gain is lost to positions kept on after the coin has bounced, not to fees.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the more a coin's volume over its last 30 days has shrunk against the 30 days before, and the closer its close still sits to its 30-day low, the more its 30-day fall carries on over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts a calm decline on drying volume only while the coin is still pressing at its lows, and stands aside once it has bounced off them.
ideas.name: volume dry-up at the lows
